liveProbe.grantInterpretation: HEAD observed SELECT endpoint behavior only. It did not inspect direct, inherited, or default GRANT catalog entries and did not test INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or EXECUTE privileges.
liveProbe.interpretation: The selected target exposes SELECT endpoints for 17 application tables and lacks five migration-010 application tables. The result does not prove policy definitions, FORCE state, ownership, mutation privileges, or cross-tenant isolation.

findings.title: Two legacy exposed-schema tables have no RLS declaration
findings.impact: If the corresponding object command privilege is granted, query text and document rows have no RLS row boundary for that command.
findings.remediation: Decide retire/operator/public intent, enable RLS, and add explicit least-privilege policies or revoke Data API privileges in an approved migration.
findings.liveValidation: HEAD observed anon SELECT endpoint reachability with zero rows for both tables; mutation privileges and effective GRANT catalog source remain unverified.

findings.title: dispatch_logs has a role-agnostic global-null CRUD branch
findings.impact: If a role has the corresponding SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE object privilege, the applicable policy accepts null-organization rows for that command.
findings.remediation: Require organization_id for tenant rows; separate operator/global events; scope tenant policies to authenticated and split CRUD.
findings.liveValidation: HEAD observed six service-role rows and zero anon-visible rows; null-row existence and mutation privileges were not tested.

findings.title: Tenant policies do not enforce same-organization relationships and service-role child queries trust them
provenEvidence: The schema allows organization_id/related-ID mismatch when ordinary FK existence checks pass because row policies validate only organization_id.
Education and dispatch APIs accept request-supplied workpack/worker related IDs without specific ownership validation.
Commercial child reads validate an owned parent and then query children by workpack_id without an additional organization_id predicate.
findings.conditionalImpact: If an authenticated role has INSERT/UPDATE object privilege, knows a foreign related UUID, and satisfies its own organization predicate, a mismatched relationship can be accepted. If such a row exists and matches a privileged child query, it could be included in that response.
findings.severityRationale: P1 retained because the proven schema gap and privileged query shape can combine at a tenant boundary; exploitability remains conditional on unverified privileges, UUID knowledge, and row existence.
findings.remediation: Add same-tenant relational constraints or checks; add organization/site predicates to privileged child queries; re-own request-supplied IDs.

findings.title: History-like tenant tables receive unrestricted owner UPDATE and DELETE
findings.impact: If authenticated has the corresponding UPDATE or DELETE object privilege, the owner FOR ALL policy permits matching history-like rows to be rewritten or deleted.
findings.remediation: Split policies by command and retain only required writes; constrain state transitions and retention deletes.
findings.liveValidation: UPDATE/DELETE object privileges and mutations were not tested.

findings.title: Ingestion-run operational metadata has an unrestricted SELECT row policy
findings.impact: If anon/authenticated has SELECT object privilege, internal report paths, failure details, and arbitrary operation metadata are row-visible.
findings.remediation: Make the table operator-only or expose a sanitized public view.
findings.liveValidation: HEAD observed two rows visible to both service-role and anon credentials; row bodies and effective GRANT catalog entries were not inspected.

findings.title: mcp_tokens tenant binding is not schema-enforced
findings.impact: Privileged paths can create orphaned, unscoped, or site/organization-mismatched credential rows.
findings.remediation: Add organization FK, valid-scope constraints, and site-to-organization consistency enforcement in an approved migration.
findings.liveValidation: HEAD observed one service-role row and zero anon-visible rows; privileged write constraints were not tested.

findings.title: Published ontology edges do not require published endpoint nodes
findings.impact: If the caller has SELECT object privilege, a published edge can be row-visible and reveal unpublished node identifiers, relations, citations, or metadata.
findings.remediation: Require both endpoint nodes to be published in workflow and SELECT enforcement, or expose a security-invoker published-only join view.
findings.liveValidation: HEAD observed 182 service-role and 169 anon-visible edge rows; endpoint-node publication consistency was not inspected.

findings.title: Tenant policies omit explicit roles and FORCE RLS
findings.impact: Role intent is implicit; object command privilege is still required before policy evaluation, and table-owner SQL remains outside RLS. FORCE would not control service_role BYPASSRLS.
findings.remediation: Use explicit TO roles and authenticated checks; separately evaluate FORCE for owner defense in depth.
findings.liveValidation: Policy roles, owners, FORCE flags, and effective GRANT catalog entries were not inspected live.

findings.title: Service-only RPC intent is not reflected in grants or function hardening
findings.impact: If a role has EXECUTE privilege, function reachability and namespace behavior rely on defaults even though invoker RLS prevents non-bypass embedding rows.
findings.remediation: Schema-qualify relations, explicitly use invoker semantics, pin search_path, and revoke/grant EXECUTE to the intended roles.
findings.liveValidation: The embedding table returned 404 and effective EXECUTE grants were not inspected.
